children.name: Thematic Coding
children.blurb: Thematic coding is the family of qualitative techniques for marking segments of text or talk with labels and then grouping those labels into broader themes.

children.name: Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation
children.blurb: Interview transcription and speaker separation covers the conversion of recorded interviews into written text and the labelling of who spoke when.

children.name: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience
children.blurb: Finding patterns in lived experience is a qualitative and mixed methods research activity.

children.name: Ethnographic Synthesis
children.blurb: Ethnographic synthesis is the work of drawing together findings from two or more ethnographic or closely observational studies into a single comparative account.

children.name: Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data
children.blurb: Combining qualitative and quantitative data, often called mixed methods, is the practice of bringing narrative, observational, or interview material together with counts, measurements, or statistical summaries in one study.

sections.body: Qualitative analysis and mixed methods is the part of AI research that deals with words, images, sounds, and lived experience rather than only numbers. In practice, AI is used to transcribe interviews, separate speakers, suggest codes, group similar passages, and surface patterns across large sets of field notes. It can also help synthesize ethnographic material by linking observations to themes and by comparing themes with survey or sensor data. The work is not about replacing the researcher's judgment. It is about handling scale, making early passes through messy material, and keeping an audit trail of how interpretations were formed. These systems are tools inside a longer interpretive process, not autonomous analysts.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of this field are now routine. Automatic speech recognition can produce usable transcripts for clear audio, and speaker separation can label turns in many interviews. Coding assistants can propose labels and retrieve similar excerpts, which speeds up first-cycle coding. What remains hard is meaning, because models often miss irony, silence, cultural reference, power dynamics, and the way a speaker changes position over time. They can overcode, flatten disagreement, and produce themes that look tidy but do not hold up against the full transcript. Mixed methods add another limit, since aligning a theme with a quantitative variable does not establish cause or explain the mechanism.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section form a path from raw material to interpretation, starting with Thematic Coding, which turns transcripts and field notes into labeled categories. Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation covers the step before that, where audio becomes text and who said what is marked. Finding Patterns in Lived Experience looks at how repeated concerns, routines, and tensions emerge across many accounts. Ethnographic Synthesis deals with combining observations, documents, and interviews into a coherent account of a setting. Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data shows how themes can be placed beside counts, scores, or sensor readings without pretending the two kinds of evidence are the same. The site's library holds 135 research papers, and these pages sit within that broader record.
